parts.latex:
Ashford ($A$), Brookdale ($B$) and Carlton ($C$) are three country towns.

Brookdale is 85 km east and 33 km north of Ashford.

Carlton is on a bearing of $026^\circ$ from Ashford and $321^\circ$ from Brookdale.

Jo completes a cross-country drive which starts and finishes in Ashford and passes through Brookdale and Carlton.

Calculate the total distance that Jo travelled, correct to the nearest kilometre.

\exfigure{510_q22_1}

solutions.latex:
By Pythagoras' theorem: $$AB=\sqrt{85^2+33^2}=91.181\ldots$$

$$\text{Angle }DAB=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{33}{85}\right)=21^\circ 13'$$

$$\text{Angle }CAB=90^\circ-26^\circ-21^\circ 13'=42^\circ 47'$$

$$\text{Angle }ACB=(360^\circ-321^\circ)+26^\circ=65^\circ\quad\text{(angles at a point and alternate angles)}$$

$$\text{Angle }ABC=180^\circ-65^\circ-42^\circ 47'=72^\circ 13'\quad\text{(angle sum of triangle }ABC\text{)}$$

By the sine rule: $$AC=\dfrac{\sin 72^\circ 13'\times 91.181}{\sin 65^\circ}=95.800$$

$$BC=\dfrac{\sin 42^\circ 47'\times 91.181}{\sin 65^\circ}=68.335$$

Alternatively, $BC$ may be determined using the cosine rule: $$BC=\sqrt{91.181^2+95.800^2-2\times 91.181\times 95.800\times\cos 42^\circ 47'}=68.335$$

Perimeter of triangle $ABC$: $$91.181+95.800+68.335=255.316$$

The total distance travelled is 255 km, correct to the nearest kilometre.
criteria: Determines the length of the other sides of triangle $ABC$ using sine or cosine rule
Finds all angles in triangle $ABC$ and distance $AB$ or equivalent merit
Finds both distance $AB$ and angle $DAB$, or equivalent merit
Finds either distance $AB$ or angle $DAB$, or equivalent merit

\exfigure{339_q15_s1}

The car's bearing is $N30^\circ W$ and the motor bike travels due east, so

$$\angle COM=30^\circ+90^\circ=120^\circ$$

After one hour, $OC=80$ km and $OM=60$ km.

By the cosine rule in $\triangle COM$:

$$\begin{aligned} CM^2 &= OC^2+OM^2-2\,OC\times OM\cos\angle COM \\ &= 80^2+60^2-2\times 80\times 60\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 80^2+60^2-2\times 80\times 60\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \\ &= 14800 \end{aligned}$$

Since $CM>0$:

$$\begin{aligned} CM &= \sqrt{14800} \\ &= \sqrt{400\times 37} \\ &= 20\sqrt{37}\text{ km} \end{aligned}$$

By the sine rule in $\triangle COM$:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin\angle CMO}{OC} &= \dfrac{\sin\angle COM}{CM} \\ \dfrac{\sin\angle CMO}{80} &= \dfrac{\sin 120^\circ}{20\sqrt{37}} \\ \sin\angle CMO &= \dfrac{80\sin 120^\circ}{20\sqrt{37}} \\ \angle CMO &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{80\sin 120^\circ}{20\sqrt{37}}\right) \\ &= 34.71500\ldots^\circ \\ &\approx 35^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Since $\angle COM=120^\circ$ is obtuse, $\angle CMO$ must be acute.

The motor bike is due east of $O$, so $O$ is due west of $M$ (bearing $270^\circ$), and $C$ lies north of $OM$.

$$\text{Bearing}=270^\circ+35^\circ=305^\circ$$

$$\therefore \text{ the bearing of the car from the motor bike is approximately } 305^\circ\text{T } (N55^\circ W)$$

Alternatively, use the cosine rule to find $\angle CMO$.

parts.latex: If $\cos\theta=\dfrac{-2}{3}$ and $\pi<\theta<\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, what is the value of $\tan\theta$?

solutions.latex:
Since $\pi<\theta<\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $\theta$ is in the third quadrant, so $\tan\theta$ is positive.

In a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $3$ and adjacent side $2$, Pythagoras' theorem gives the opposite side:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{opposite} &= \sqrt{3^2-2^2} \\ &= \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Given that $\sin\theta=\dfrac{6+\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{19}}$ and $\theta$ is obtuse, find the exact value of $\tan\theta$ in simplest form.

solutions.latex:
Since $\theta$ is obtuse, it lies in quadrant 2, so $\sin\theta>0$ and $\tan\theta<0$. Construct a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $2\sqrt{19}$ and opposite side $6+\sqrt{2}$.

\exfigure{1309_q24_s1}

Let $A$ be the adjacent side. By Pythagoras' theorem:
$$\begin{aligned} A^2 &= \left(2\sqrt{19}\right)^2-\left(6+\sqrt{2}\right)^2 \\ &= 76-\left(36+12\sqrt{2}+2\right) \\ &= 76-\left(38+12\sqrt{2}\right) \\ &= 38-12\sqrt{2} \\ &= 36-12\sqrt{2}+2 \\ &= \left(6-\sqrt{2}\right)^2 \end{aligned}$$
so $A=6-\sqrt{2}$.

In quadrant 2 the tangent is negative:
$$\therefore\ \tan\theta=-\dfrac{6+\sqrt{2}}{6-\sqrt{2}}$$
or equivalently
$$\tan\theta=\dfrac{6+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}-6}$$

parts.latex: What is the value of $\tan x$ given that $\sin x=\dfrac{1}{3}$ for $\dfrac{\pi}{2}<x<\pi$.

solutions.latex:
Since $\dfrac{\pi}{2}<x<\pi$, $x$ is in the second quadrant, so $\cos x<0$.

Using $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned} \cos^2 x &= 1-\dfrac{1}{9}=\dfrac{8}{9} \\ \cos x &= -\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} \end{aligned}$$
Then
$$\begin{aligned} \tan x &= \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{3}\times\left(-\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) \\ &= -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \end{aligned}$$
This is option A.
